title: Dealing with Travel Delays
objectives: Understand and use vocabulary related to travel disruptions including cancelled, delayed, rescheduled, and diverted
Ask transit or airline staff clear questions about delays and rebooking options
Communicate travel delays to an employer, family member, or appointment
Evaluate options and make decisions when travel plans change unexpectedly

reading_passage.title: When Planes and Buses Don't Run on Time
reading_passage.text:
Travel disruptions are an unavoidable part of life. Whether it is a bus that fails to show up on a rainy morning or an international flight delayed by mechanical issues, unexpected delays can cause real problems — missed appointments, late arrivals at work, or added costs for rebooking.

For air travellers in the United States, airlines are required by federal regulations to compensate passengers under certain conditions. If an airline cancels your flight and it was their fault — not due to weather or other circumstances beyond their control — you are entitled to a full refund, even on a non-refundable ticket. Some airlines will also offer meal vouchers or hotel accommodation if the delay is lengthy. However, these rules do not apply to delays caused by severe weather, which are classified as 'extraordinary circumstances.'

For bus and train passengers, the rules differ. Public transit agencies typically do not offer compensation for delays, but they may provide information about alternative routes. In the event of a service disruption on the MAX light rail in Portland, for example, TriMet often runs shuttle buses to cover the affected segment of the route.

The most important thing any traveller can do during a delay is to stay informed. Check the airline or transit agency's app or website for real-time updates. Speak with staff at the information desk rather than waiting passively. If a long delay is unavoidable, notify anyone expecting you — your employer, a medical clinic, a host family — as early as possible.
reading_passage.source: Adapted from U.S. Department of Transportation consumer travel tips and the TriMet Service Alerts page, 2024

glossary.meaning: an unexpected interruption that prevents normal service or plans from continuing
to give money or other benefits to someone as payment for a loss or inconvenience
a printed or digital token that can be exchanged for a specific product or service
events beyond anyone's control, such as severe weather, that excuse an airline from paying compensation
a bus that runs on a temporary route to replace another service that is not operating

comprehension.question: Under what condition is an airline required to give a full refund for a cancelled flight?
comprehension.answer: When the airline cancelled the flight and it was their fault — not due to weather or other circumstances beyond their control.

comprehension.question: What does the author imply when they say 'weather delays are classified as extraordinary circumstances'?
comprehension.answer: The author implies that in these cases, the airline is not legally responsible for compensating passengers — the delay is not the airline's fault, so different rules apply.

comprehension.question: What does the word 'compensate' mean in paragraph two?
comprehension.answer: To give passengers money or other benefits (such as a refund or vouchers) because they suffered a loss or inconvenience due to the airline's fault.

comprehension.question: Why does the author advise travellers to notify anyone expecting them 'as early as possible'?
comprehension.answer: Because informing people early gives them time to adjust their plans — an employer can arrange cover, a clinic can reschedule an appointment, and a host can make alternative arrangements.

language_focus.title: First Conditional for Likely Outcomes (If + present simple, will + verb)
language_focus.explanation: The first conditional is used to describe likely or realistic situations and their probable outcomes. It follows the pattern: 'If [present simple], [will + base verb].' This is especially useful when discussing travel disruptions — what will happen if a flight is delayed, what you will do if you miss a connection, and so on.

examples.sentence: If the bus doesn't arrive in the next five minutes, I will take a taxi instead.
examples.note: The condition is realistic and possible — the outcome (taking a taxi) is the likely response.

examples.sentence: If the airline cancels your flight, they will offer you a full refund or a rebooking.
examples.note: The condition (cancellation) is possible; the outcome (refund or rebooking) is what typically follows under the rules.

practice.sentence: Rewrite using first conditional: 'The flight might be delayed. I will notify my employer.'
practice.answer: If the flight is delayed, I will notify my employer.

practice.sentence: Complete this conditional: 'If I miss the connecting bus, ___.'
practice.answer: If I miss the connecting bus, I will ask staff about the next available service. (Accept other logical completions.)

practice.sentence: Which is correct? A) If the train will be late, I will call you. B) If the train is late, I will call you.
practice.answer: B) In the first conditional, the 'if' clause uses present simple (not 'will') — 'If the train is late, I will call you.'

vocabulary_in_context.definition: Something unexpected that interrupts normal service or plans
vocabulary_in_context.example_sentence: In the event of a service disruption on the MAX light rail in Portland, TriMet often runs shuttle buses.

vocabulary_in_context.definition: To give money, vouchers, or services to someone as payment for a loss or inconvenience
vocabulary_in_context.example_sentence: Airlines are required by federal regulations to compensate passengers under certain conditions.

vocabulary_in_context.definition: A document or digital code that can be exchanged for a specific product, service, or discount
vocabulary_in_context.example_sentence: Some airlines will also offer meal vouchers or hotel accommodation if the delay is lengthy.

speaking_task.context: Your flight has been cancelled and you are at the airline information desk at the airport. The delay is not due to weather — it is a mechanical problem with the plane.
speaking_task.prompt: Speak to the airline employee. Ask what happened, find out what your options are (rebooking or refund), ask about compensation such as meal vouchers, and confirm when the next available flight leaves. Use first conditional sentences where appropriate.
useful_language: Could you tell me why the flight has been cancelled?
If I take the next available flight, will you rebook me at no extra cost?
Am I entitled to any compensation, such as a meal voucher or accommodation?
speaking_task.model_answer: Excuse me — I'm booked on flight 447 to Seattle, which I can see has been cancelled. Could you explain what happened? Since it's a mechanical issue, am I entitled to compensation? If the next available flight leaves this evening, will you rebook me without any additional charge? And if the delay is more than three hours, would it be possible to get a meal voucher while I wait?

writing_workshop.model_text:
Subject: Running Late Due to Bus Delay

Hello Ms. Rivera,

I wanted to let you know that I will be late to work this morning. The 72 bus has been delayed due to a service disruption on the route. I am currently at the stop on Division Street. If the situation does not improve in the next ten minutes, I will take a rideshare instead. I expect to arrive by 9:30 at the latest. I apologise for the inconvenience and will make up the time at the end of the shift.

Thank you,
Abdirahman
writing_workshop.model_analysis: Notice how the writer immediately explains the situation, gives a specific timeline, offers an alternative plan, and apologises professionally — all important elements of a work communication during a delay.
writing_workshop.task: Write a short message (email or text) to an employer or a medical clinic explaining that you will be late due to a travel delay. Include what happened, when you expect to arrive, and what alternative plan you have if the situation gets worse.
success_criteria: Clearly state the reason for the delay in the first sentence
Use at least one first conditional sentence (if... will...)
Include a specific estimated arrival time and a brief apology

quiz.question: According to the passage, when is a passenger entitled to a full refund from an airline?
options: Any time a flight is delayed by more than one hour
When a flight is cancelled due to a weather emergency
When an airline cancels a flight and it is the airline's fault
Only if the passenger purchased travel insurance
quiz.explanation: The passage states: 'If an airline cancels your flight and it was their fault — not due to weather or other circumstances beyond their control — you are entitled to a full refund.'

quiz.question: What does TriMet do when there is a service disruption on the MAX light rail?
options: Cancels all services for the day
Refunds all affected passengers
Runs shuttle buses to cover the affected route segment
Directs passengers to use rideshare services
quiz.explanation: The passage says: 'TriMet often runs shuttle buses to cover the affected segment of the route.'

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly uses the first conditional?
options: If the bus will be late, I will take a taxi.
If the bus is late, I will take a taxi.
If the bus is late, I would take a taxi.
If the bus was late, I will take a taxi.
quiz.explanation: The first conditional requires present simple in the 'if' clause ('is late') and 'will + base verb' in the result clause ('will take').

quiz.question: What does the passage recommend travellers do first when a delay occurs?
options: File a formal complaint with the transport authority
Stay informed by checking apps, websites, and speaking with staff
Immediately book an alternative route without checking the original
Wait quietly and trust that the problem will resolve itself
quiz.explanation: The final paragraph says: 'The most important thing any traveller can do during a delay is to stay informed. Check the airline or transit agency's app or website for real-time updates.'

listening_exercises.transcript: Attention passengers: flight six-one-two to Denver is delayed due to bad weather. The new departure time is seven forty-five PM. We apologize for the inconvenience. If you have a connecting flight, please speak to an agent at the customer service desk. Passengers may also rebook for free on tomorrow morning's flight using our mobile app.
listening_exercises.question: What can passengers with a connecting flight do?
options: Wait at the gate
Speak to an agent at the customer service desk
Board the plane early
Ask the pilot for help

listening_exercises.transcript: When your bus or train is late, stay calm and check the information screens first. Announcements will usually explain the delay and give a new time. If you might miss an important appointment, call ahead and explain the situation — most offices understand transportation delays. Keep your ticket, because some companies give refunds when a delay is very long.
listening_exercises.question: Why should you keep your ticket during a long delay?
options: To board first
Some companies give refunds
To get free food
The driver will ask for it twice
